findings.title: Your two highest-intent pages have zero internal links pointing at them
findings.evidence: /compare/pocketprep-alternative — 0 inbound internal links. /compare/best-pmp-exam-simulator-2026 — 0 inbound internal links. /about — 0. Measured by parsing every <a href> on all 23 crawled pages. Both compare pages are in the sitemap, so Google can find them; nothing on the site tells Google they matter.
findings.why: These are the only two pages you own that target buying-decision queries. An orphan page inherits no authority from the homepage's 189 inbound links, and orphan status is one of the clearest low-priority signals you can send.
findings.fix: Add a 'Compare' entry to the primary nav or footer linking both pages. Link /compare/best-pmp-exam-simulator-2026 from /lp/pmp and from the two PMP blog posts. Link /compare/pocketprep-alternative from /pricing and from /exam-lens. Link /about from the footer and from every post's author line.
findings.resolution: Shipped 2026-09-03. Re-crawl: /compare/best-pmp-exam-simulator-2026 34 inbound, /compare/pocketprep-alternative 18, /about 15. Footer sitewide, mobile nav, and in-body links from /lp/pmp, /lp/security-plus, /pricing, /exam-lens and two articles.

findings.title: Three of four landing pages have two internal links each
findings.evidence: Inbound internal links: /lp/pmp 8, /lp/security-plus 2, /lp/network-plus 2, /lp/a-plus-core-2 2. Those two are the homepage cert selector and the footer.
findings.why: Landing pages are the conversion surface for the exact queries you want. At two inbound links they read as leaf pages, not destinations. This mirrors the funnel: the September landscape scan measured 4,525 of 4,832 impressions on PMP and 307 on Security+. The internal link graph is reinforcing the same imbalance rather than correcting it.
findings.fix: Build a /certifications hub that links all four LPs with 40–60 words of unique context each, link the hub from the nav, and add a contextual in-body link from every blog post to the LP for the cert that post uses as its worked example.

findings.title: /terms and /privacy emit the homepage's title, description and canonical
findings.evidence: Both pages return title 'CipherExam — Learn How Certification Exams Think', the homepage's 206-character description, and rel=canonical pointing at https://cipherexam.com/ — not at themselves. Their H1s are correct ('Terms of Service', 'Privacy Policy'). Both are listed in sitemap.xml.
findings.why: Two things are wrong at once. The canonical tells Google these pages are the homepage, so they will be dropped from the index while sitting in your sitemap — a direct contradiction Search Console reports as an error. And the fallback proves the page template has a default-meta path that silently applies when a route forgets to set its own. Any future page that forgets will inherit the same bug.
findings.fix: Set self-referencing canonicals and page-specific title/description on both routes. Then make the default a build-time failure rather than a silent fallback, so the next page cannot repeat it.
findings.resolution: Shipped 2026-09-03. Both pages render SeoHead with SEO.terms / SEO.privacy; re-crawl confirms self-canonical and page-specific titles.

findings.title: The four landing pages have visible FAQ sections and no FAQPage schema
findings.evidence: All four /lp/ pages render an H2 'Frequently asked'. Their JSON-LD contains only Organization and WebSite. /pricing and both /compare pages do carry FAQPage — so the pattern exists in the codebase and was simply not applied here.
findings.why: This is the single highest-return schema change available. Question-answer pairs are what AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity extract most reliably, and the answers are already written. You are leaving the markup off finished content.
findings.fix: Emit FAQPage JSON-LD from the same data that renders the visible FAQ block, on all four LPs. Reuse the /pricing implementation.
findings.resolution: Shipped 2026-09-03. New LpFaq.tsx feeds the visible <dl> and the FAQPage JSON-LD from one array per LP. Re-crawl: all four LPs emit FAQPage; /lp/pmp schema and visible questions identical (6/6), answers free of markup.

findings.title: No Google Search Console feedback loop
findings.evidence: No GSC data was available to this audit, and nothing in the repo references a Search Console property or export. The competitor-intel funnel numbers come from GA4 (property 528695114) and graded post impressions — social, not search.
findings.why: Every recommendation in this report is a hypothesis about what search wants. Without query-level data you cannot tell a page that ranks at position 11 from one that has never been seen, and those need opposite responses. This is the cheapest high-leverage action on the list.
findings.fix: Verify cipherexam.com in Search Console today. Submit the sitemap. Wait 28 days, then export queries and pages and wire the CSV into this tab the way GA4 clicks already are (scripts/pull-ga4-clicks.mjs is the pattern).

findings.title: Unknown URLs return HTTP 200 instead of 404
findings.evidence: Probed /this-page-does-not-exist-xyz, /lp/shrm-cp, /lp/pmp-practice, /compare, /llms.txt, /feed.xml, /rss.xml — every one returned status 200 with an HTML shell, 10.7 KB, no H1, 275 words. Mitigating factor found: that shell does emit robots 'noindex,nofollow,noarchive', so the pages will not be indexed.
findings.why: The noindex saves you from the worst outcome. What remains is crawl waste on an unbounded URL space and a Soft 404 report in Search Console once it is connected. Note that three of those probed paths — /lp/pmp-practice, /lp/security-plus-practice, /lp/shrm-cp — are the LP routes still documented as locked in README.md and 00-campaign-brief.md. The live routes are /lp/pmp, /lp/security-plus, /lp/network-plus, /lp/a-plus-core-2. Any campaign asset built from the old brief points at a dead URL.
findings.fix: Return a real 404 status for unmatched routes. Separately, correct the LP routes in README.md and the campaign brief so no future post links a dead path.

findings.title: Six meta descriptions and three titles are longer than search will display
findings.evidence: Descriptions over ~160 characters: / 206, /compare/best-pmp-exam-simulator-2026 275, /exam-lens 227, /compare/pocketprep-alternative 218, /lp/a-plus-core-2 188, /lp/network-plus 187, /blog/pmp-exam-changes-july-2026 271. Titles over ~60 characters: /compare/best-pmp-exam-simulator-2026 70, /blog/pmp-exam-changes-july-2026 70, /lp/a-plus-core-2 69.
findings.why: Truncation is not a ranking penalty, it is a click-through penalty. The homepage description loses the free-trial offer — the strongest thing in it — because it sits past character 160.
findings.fix: Rewrite to 150–160 characters for descriptions and 50–60 for titles, front-loading the offer and the cert name. Add a build-time length check so this cannot regress.

findings.title: Every article declares dateModified equal to datePublished, while the sitemap says all 23 URLs changed today
findings.evidence: Sampled Article schema on /blog/study-by-blooms-level: datePublished 2026-05-12, dateModified 2026-05-12. sitemap.xml gives lastmod 2026-09-03 for all 23 URLs including posts published in April and May.
findings.why: The two freshness signals contradict each other, so neither is trusted. A lastmod that is identical across every URL is a generated timestamp, not a change record, and crawlers learn to ignore it. Freshness matters more than usual for you: your best commercial post is about the July 2026 PMP outline change, and that page's credibility depends on looking maintained.
findings.fix: Emit lastmod from real content-change dates and update dateModified when a post is substantively revised. Do not touch either without an actual edit — date-only updates are counterproductive.

findings.title: The Organization entity has no sameAs, and its logo points at favicon.png
findings.evidence: Organization JSON-LD carries name, url, description and founder Person 'Dave Quillman'. No sameAs array. logo is https://cipherexam.com/favicon.png.
findings.why: sameAs is how you tell Google and the answer engines that the CipherExam on your site, the LinkedIn page, the X account and the Q-Code brand are one entity. Without it you are an unconnected string. Google's publisher logo guidance also expects a real logo image, not a favicon.
findings.fix: Add sameAs with your LinkedIn company page, X profile and any other owned profile. Point logo at a dedicated logo image of at least 112x112px. Add an author Person @id with its own sameAs and link it from every Article.

findings.title: The EEAT pages are the thinnest pages on the site, and one of them is orphaned
findings.evidence: /about — 615 words, zero H2s, 0 inbound internal links, Organization schema only. /story — 641 words, zero H2s. Both are shorter than every blog post.
findings.why: You are a solo founder shipping AI-assisted content into a category where a direct competitor markets its questions as 'written by humans rather than by AI' — that attack is recorded in your own battlecard, and it lands on the trust axis. About and Story are where that gets answered, and right now they are the least developed pages you have.
findings.fix: Rebuild /about into a real entity page: who builds this, what the method is, how questions are produced and reviewed, who reviews them, contact route. Add an author page for Dave Quillman with credentials and sameAs, and link it from every post byline. If a credentialed reviewer signs off on cert content, name them — that is the direct counter.

findings.title: www.cipherexam.com serves a 200 duplicate instead of redirecting
findings.evidence: https://www.cipherexam.com/ loads the full homepage and declares rel=canonical https://cipherexam.com/. No redirect was returned.
findings.why: The cross-host canonical does the job, so this is not urgent. A 301 is still the stronger, unambiguous signal and removes a whole duplicate crawl surface.
findings.fix: 301 the www host to the apex.

findings.title: Missing alt text, and every article shares one social image
findings.evidence: At least one image without an alt attribute on every crawled page; the homepage has 2 of 4. All nine Article schema blocks set image to https://cipherexam.com/og-default.png.
findings.why: Accessibility first, image search second. The shared og-default image also means every post shares one link preview, which flattens click-through anywhere your posts are shared — which is your only working channel right now.
findings.fix: Alt text on all content images. A per-post OG image; the Remotion pipeline in this repo already renders post cards and can produce them.

findings.title: No llms.txt and no RSS feed
findings.evidence: Probed /llms.txt, /feed.xml, /rss.xml, /blog/rss.xml — all returned the noindex shell, not a feed. robots.txt contains no GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot or Google-Extended directives, so AI crawlers are allowed by default.
findings.why: Allowing the AI crawlers is the right call for a site that wants to be cited, and you already are. llms.txt is a cheap, low-risk way to hand answer engines a clean map of your best pages. RSS still feeds aggregators and newsletter tools.
findings.fix: Publish /llms.txt listing the homepage, /exam-lens, the four LPs, both compare pages and the nine posts with one-line descriptions. Add /rss.xml for the blog.

blind_spots: Timeline. SEO is a 6–12 month channel. Your measured position is 1 activated user with paid capped at $2/day. Nothing in this plan moves activation this quarter, and treating it as if it will is the fastest way to abandon it at month four — which is exactly when it starts working.

The free-questions decision is a product decision, not a marketing one. Every SERP checked is won by pages giving questions away. Doing this means putting real questions with real reasoning outside the paywall. If you are not willing to, say so now and cut Wave 2 — but then accept that top-of-funnel search is closed to you and the channel is buyer-intent pages only.

Links are the binding constraint, not on-page work. Two of your four target SERPs are owned by affiliate roundups. You can execute every fix in this report perfectly and still not rank, because the winning pages have domain authority you do not have. Budget real effort for placement in those roundups.

EEAT is your exposed flank. Solo founder, AI-assisted content, in a category where a competitor is explicitly attacking AI-written material. A named credentialed reviewer is the highest-value hire-or-favour on this list, and it is not a marketing task.

Every priority here is a hypothesis until Search Console is connected. If one page is already ranking at position 11 for something valuable, that page deserves everything and this list is wrong. Twenty minutes of setup buys the right to be confident. Do it first.

crawl.legend: Baseline measured 2026-09-03 from the live HTML; inbound-link, JSON-LD and canonical columns re-measured after the 2026-09-03 deploy. status was 200 for all 23. selfCanonical false means the page canonicals somewhere else.

priority.scoring_note: Points are from the same six-dimension rubric that produced the baseline 63. Each dimension is worth 10; the overall score is the sum of the six divided by 60. One dimension point is worth 1.7 overall points. These are my rubric, not Google's — they measure whether the site is built correctly, not whether it ranks. Ranking is decided by links and content, which is why the highest-traffic items on this list are worth zero points. Items marked shipped were verified live by re-crawl and are already in the score.
priority.ceiling_note: 95 is the realistic ceiling from on-site work alone. The last 5 points are links and published content compounding over months — you cannot patch your way there in a sprint.

actions.why: The noindex header saves you from indexed junk, so this is crawl waste rather than a crisis. The documentation half is the real bug: any post built from the current brief links a dead URL.

actions.title: Make CipherExam a resolvable entity — sameAs and a real logo
steps: Add sameAs to Organization: LinkedIn company page, X profile, any other owned profile
Point logo at a dedicated image of at least 112×112px, not favicon.png
Give the author Person an @id and its own sameAs, referenced from every Article
actions.why: Without sameAs you are an unconnected string rather than a known entity. This is how Google and the answer engines learn that the site, the LinkedIn page and the X account are one thing.

actions.title: Make the freshness signals mean something
steps: Emit sitemap lastmod from real content-change dates, not the build timestamp
Update dateModified only when a post is substantively revised
Revise /blog/pmp-exam-changes-july-2026 now and let both dates move honestly
actions.why: Right now every article says dateModified equals datePublished while the sitemap claims all 23 URLs changed today. The two signals contradict each other so neither is trusted. Do not touch dates without a real edit — date-only updates are counterproductive.

actions.title: 301 www.cipherexam.com to the apex
steps: Add a permanent redirect from the www host to https://cipherexam.com
Confirm with a request that does not follow redirects
actions.why: The cross-host canonical is doing the job today, so this is cheap insurance rather than a fire. A 301 removes a whole duplicate crawl surface unambiguously.

actions.title: Ship two free, indexable practice pages
steps: /practice/pmp-questions — 20+ real questions with the full reasoning shown, free and crawlable
/practice/security-plus-pbq — a working PBQ demo, free and crawlable
CTA below the content, never gating it
Link both from the homepage, the matching LP and /certifications
actions.why: Every SERP I checked is won by free-question pages, and you have none. This is also a product decision, not a marketing one: it means putting real questions with real reasoning outside the paywall. If the answer is no, cut this item and accept that top-of-funnel search is closed to you.

actions.title: Finish the schema set
steps: BreadcrumbList on the LPs, both /compare pages and /pricing
Switch /pricing from Product to SoftwareApplication with applicationCategory and the existing Offers
ItemList on /blog
actions.why: Product without review or rating markup gets limited rich-result treatment; SoftwareApplication fits a SaaS app and is valid without inventing reviews. Breadcrumbs already work on your blog — the pattern just is not applied to the commercial pages.

actions.title: Cite primary sources, publish llms.txt and RSS
steps: Name and link the PMI Examination Content Outline and the CompTIA objectives PDFs in every relevant post
Rewrite each post's opening to lead with the answer, then explain
Publish /llms.txt listing the homepage, /exam-lens, four LPs, two compare pages and nine posts with one-line descriptions
Publish /rss.xml for the blog
actions.why: Citations are the biggest AEO lever for a cert-prep site — answer engines weight sourced claims heavily — and they double as the defence against the AI-written attack. llms.txt and RSS are an afternoon each.

actions.tier: Weeks 5–12 — no rubric points, highest traffic upside
actions.title: Content and links: the part the score cannot measure
steps: /blog/pmp-study-plan-30-days and /blog/security-plus-study-plan-30-days — cert-specific beats your generic study-plan post
/compare/examcert-alternative — ExamCert is the #2 threat in the September scan and you have no page for it
Network+ and A+ Core 2 support posts — their first ever
Repoint the outreach module at roundup editors: rebelsguidetopm, ais-cpa, open-exam-prep, prepforcerts
Exam-code pages for SY0-701, N10-009, 220-1102
actions.why: Zero points and the most valuable block on the list. Two of your four target SERPs are owned by affiliate roundups, so getting listed inside them beats out-ranking them. A perfect 95 with no links still does not rank — which is the honest limit of everything above.
